clue.text: Plain girl goes to party with navy chap

parts.note: Una is a girl's name

RN stands for Royal Navy

explanation.surface: A dowdy girl heads off to a party with a sailor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Plain' sits as an insult to the girl but is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Something plain has no decoration or ornament, a straightforward synonym.

clue.text: See US right-winger gas, enthralling company

clue.text: Lost initially in games, then was finally second to none

finally takes the last letter of was

explanation.definitionFit: Matchless means without equal, peerless.

clue.text: Notice revolutionary leftie, wicked and extremely reckless

clue.text: One who demonstrates in favour of someone doing experiments?

parts.note: pro means in favour of
a tester is someone who carries out tests

explanation.surface: A demonstrator is described as a supporter of scientists.
explanation.walkthrough: 'demonstrates' suggests showing how something works; it is marching in protest.
explanation.definitionFit: A protester takes part in demonstrations, campaigning against something.

clue.text: Marketplace almost sounds weird

parts.note: bizarre means weird or strange

explanation.surface: Someone remarks that a trading place seems a little odd.
explanation.definitionFit: A bazaar is an oriental market, a place of stalls and traders.

clue.text: Plant a shrub with berries — then have some wine

hock is a German white wine from the Rhine

explanation.surface: Gardening advice: plant a berry bush, then reward yourself with a glass.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Plant' looks like an instruction to the gardener, but it is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The hollyhock is a tall flowering garden plant of the mallow family.

clue.text: Perhaps a grave mishap — I had to escape

explanation.definitionFit: A grave is one example of a diacritical accent, so the definition is by example with 'Perhaps'.

clue.text: A hole most dreadfully repulsive

indicators.note: dreadfully signals the letters of the three words are badly treated and rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone complains that a particular dwelling is grim beyond words.
explanation.definitionFit: Loathsome and repulsive are synonyms, both meaning disgusting.

clue.text: Runs in British city

parts.note: Leeds is a city in Yorkshire, northern England

explanation.walkthrough: 'Runs' reads as jogging; it is the verb for dye or blood seeping out.
explanation.definitionFit: Colours that run on washing are said to bleed, a verb synonym.

clue.text: Bill locks performers in theatre maybe

parts.note: AC is short for account, a bill

clue.text: Medical preparation Mary found in hospital department

clue.text: First thing for batsman after game is massage

..., rest in peace, is the parting words on a gravestone

clue.text: Desert? Not I — the reverse!

Not drops the letter I from the desert's name

parts.note: the Gobi is a desert in Asia

explanation.walkthrough: The opposite of a desert, a dry place, is a wet marsh, so the whole clue also defines.
explanation.definitionFit: A bog is soggy marshland, the wet reverse of an arid desert.

clue.text: Hero in is Cameron, struggling no matter what?

indicators.note: struggling indicates the letters of these words are in disarray and must be rearranged

explanation.surface: A political sketch: a hero has entered, and David Cameron, the former British prime minister, is in difficulty.

clue.text: Animal good with Indian boy cast adrift

clue.text: Wave from posh car

definitions.meaning: a long heavy sea wave is called a ...

clue.text: After party upset good-looking girl is somewhat strange

clue.text: Star has time in a beastly home
